requirement:
Each correction MUST carry a nonempty Markdown rationale identifying the
obligation and explaining why the observed evidence warrants that change.
For `AddReference`, explain how the item serves the proposed role. For `Manual`,
explain the gap the instruction would close.
rationale:
structural: The structural obligation in `requirements.authoring.corrections.rationale` is that every correction carries a rationale and that it is nonempty. An alternative that stored no rationale on a correction would violate the clause "Each correction MUST carry a nonempty Markdown rationale".

- `src/authoring/corrections.rs#enum[Correction]` declares `rationale: String` on both variants, `AddReference` and `Manual`. It uses `deny_unknown_fields` with the serde tag `kind`, so the field is part of the schema and the serialized form. It is not optional or defaulted, so deserialization fails if it is missing. The `{impl}` markers on this enum are justified.
- `src/authoring/corrections.rs#impl[AssessmentResult]/fn[evidence]` rejects any `Failed` result unless each correction has a rationale that is not blank after `trim()`. This check runs for both `Manual` and `AddReference`. The error is returned as `io::Error`, so a result with an empty rationale is not accepted. The `{impl}` marker on this function is justified.

The remaining clauses are about content: the rationale must identify the obligation, explain why the evidence warrants the change, explain how the item serves the proposed role for `AddReference`, and explain the gap for `Manual`. These describe what the author writes. They do not prescribe any code structure, and code cannot enforce them beyond the nonempty check already present. They need no further implementation roots.

behavioral: The only mechanically observable obligation in `requirements.authoring.corrections.rationale` is that every correction, `AddReference` or `Manual`, carries a nonempty rationale. The tests cover this.

- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[malformed_definition_corrections_can_be_repaired_before_writing_evidence]` submits malformed `failed` results. The cases include a `manual` correction with a whitespace-only rationale and one with no rationale. They also include an `add_reference` correction with no rationale, one with an empty rationale and one with a whitespace-only rationale. In each case the submission is rejected and a tool message returns to the assessor. A repaired `successful_review` then completes with determination `true` and evidence is written only after that. So missing, empty and blank rationales are rejected for both correction kinds.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[corrections_replay_reference_only_mixed_and_regression_findings]` submits valid corrections of both kinds with nonempty rationales. The `mixed` case asserts that the persisted `corrections` list equals the submitted `manual` and `add_reference` corrections, so each rationale is preserved. It also asserts that both rationales appear in the record rationale in order.

The requirement also asks that the rationale identify the obligation and explain why the evidence warrants the change. It asks that an `AddReference` rationale explain how the item serves the role, and that a `Manual` rationale explain the gap. These are qualities of free-text content that the assessor writes. The program cannot check them deterministically, so I found no further observable obligation that needs its own test.

I found no unmet obligation, so I report no gaps.
